When Should Your Child See an Orthodontist? You don't always have to wait until all of your child's permanent teeth have erupted before seeing an orthodontist. For some children, an orthodontic evaluation between 6 and 10 years of age can help identify growth and bite concerns at an important stage of development. Look out for signs such as: Mouth breathing or frequent snoring Crowded or misplaced teeth Crossbite A narrow upper jaw Concerns with the bite or jaw growth Early evaluation doesn't necessarily mean your child needs braces. It allows an orthodontist to monitor development and, when appropriate, guide jaw growth or use expansion while your child is still growing. If something doesn't look right with your child's bite, jaw, teeth, or breathing, don't wait for all the permanent teeth to come in. An early checkup can help identify problems while there is still an opportunity to guide growth. Want to know the 5 signs your child may need an orthodontic checkup? How long does Invisalign really take? The answer isn’t the same for everyone. Your treatment timeline depends on two things: where your smile starts and where you want it to finish. From minor alignment changes to more complex bite and tooth movements, every Invisalign journey is different. That’s why your friend’s 6-month treatment doesn’t necessarily mean yours will take 6 months too.
